module purpose: neorv32_hwspinlock implements 32 clocked lock bits behind a bus request/response record interface. Lower-range addressed accesses update one selected lock bit with `not bus_req_i.rw`, reads return either the selected lock bit or the full lock vector, and the response logic acknowledges each strobe.

use-case flows.value: selected lock bit updated to `not bus_req_i.rw` on a lower-range addressed access
stored lock state returned as either `lock_q and sel` or the full `lock_q` vector on read accesses
bus response acknowledge mirrors the request strobe and error is forced low
all lock bits cleared to '0' and the bus response forced to constant `rsp_terminate_c` while `rstn_i = '0'`

conceptual assets.concept: Held spinlock state -- the 32 lock bits that record which locks are set
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each generated register bit is cleared on reset (lines 41-42) and, on a rising edge, a lower-range selected access stores `not bus_req_i.rw` into `lock_q(i)` when `bus_req_i.stb = '1'`, `bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0'` and `sel(i) = '1'` (lines 43-45, with selection from line 51). Readback depends on the same state: lower-range reads return `lock_q and sel` (line 68) and the alternate range returns `lock_q` (line 70) under the read condition of lines 66-67. Integrity is established because corrupting this stored state changes both the acquire/release result and the reported lock status; availability is also established because the state is held between clocked updates and is returned on reads. The request/response ports are transport records, so the internal store is the eligible structural reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Address-decoded lock selection -- the one-hot decision of which lock index a lower-range access targets
conceptual assets.reasoning: `sel(i)` is computed as '1' when `bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2)` equals the generated index and '0' otherwise (line 51; map record GATED_BY bus_req_i.addr). That decision is used in the write-side condition `... and (sel(i) = '1')` to choose which `lock_q(i)` updates (line 44), and in `bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel` to return only the selected lock on lower-range reads (line 68). Integrity is established because a wrong selection decision updates or reports the wrong lock bit; availability is also established because the decoder produces the selection from the current address. The addressed bus field itself is part of a transport port and is not reportable, so the internal decoder `sel` is the eligible structural reference.
